description.narrative: Corruption is a structural deep-rooted challenge in Yemen, accentuated by the intricate nexus between corruption and conflict. Costs go well beyond financial loss and are visible in the dismal state of human development, and the opportunities lost for a better future. Yemen had ratified the UNCAC in 2005 and made key steps to implement it; however, these efforts have hit a standstill since 2014. The opportunity to restart them is now revived thanks to the recent steps taken by the IRG; however, key challenges remain, including limited financial resources, political interference, security threats, and major institutional gaps. To advance anti-corruption in a manner that builds on the newly generated momentum, while accounting for related risks, the proposal adopts an incremental, adaptive and people-centred approach to achieve three outputs over a period of 12 months: • Coordinated gender-balanced capacities established to support the development, implementation, and reporting on anti-corruption policies and programmes at national, local and sectoral levels. • A gender-informed strategic framework on integrity for recovery in Yemen developed through a multi-stakeholder process. • An inclusive women-led network established and empowered to monitor the implementation of the strategic framework on integrity for recovery and advocate for promoting the gender and corruption nexus.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
